items.title: August Laurent Interview, 1960-03-21
items.q: The interviewee refers to 'his brother' in the third person ('He lived on Monroir Street... his brother moved to St. Menard Street'). The interviewee does not claim to be the brother, nor does he describe a personal relationship with the brother, only narrating the brother's actions and location rel

ctx.x: On Oakwood Street, yeah. He lived on Monroir Street. Then they moved to, his brother moved to St. Menard Street, but his brother got rid of him then. He moved to St. Menard and Moray. And from St. Menard and Moray he moved to St. Menard and Villaray.
His brother of course was always proud of him in the late years. Yes, in the late years.

But no, you know when he got proud of him? When I picked him up at the airport and brought him to my house. After that, yeah. Then his brother came up to the house and had supper with him that night. That's when he started to begin to work. But I'm the one picking him up at the airport. That's his first trip back here in twenty some years.
